---
title: "A click-through Manim scene"
description: "Write a Manim scene that advances one idea per click and looks like part of the slide."
---

This guide writes a Manim scene for a talk: steps that follow the speaker,
short and direct motion, and colors that match the slide.

## One step per idea

`self.next_section()` starts a new step. With `Manim(..., interactive=True)`,
each step waits for a click, so the speaker decides when the next idea appears:

```python
from banners import BLUE, Manim, Section
from manim import DOWN, RIGHT, Arrow, FadeIn, GrowArrow, RoundedRectangle, Scene, VGroup, rate_functions
from manim import Text as MText

class Pipeline(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        names = ["Ingest", "Clean", "Train"]
        boxes = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(
                RoundedRectangle(width=2.4, height=1, corner_radius=0.12,
                                 color=BLUE.primary, fill_opacity=0.15),
                MText(name, font_size=26, color=BLUE.text),
            )
            for name in names
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.2)
        for i, box in enumerate(boxes):
            self.next_section(f"step_{i}")
            parts = [FadeIn(box, shift=RIGHT * 0.15)]
            if i:
                parts.append(GrowArrow(Arrow(boxes[i - 1].get_right(), box.get_left(),
                                             buff=0.1, color=BLUE.muted)))
            self.play(*parts, run_time=0.25, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_out_cubic)

Section(title="Our pipeline", content=[Manim(Pipeline, interactive=True)], palette=BLUE)
```

## Rules that make a scene present well

- **One change per click.** Each step shows one new idea; the audience reads
  it while the speaker talks.
- **Short steps.** Between 0.2 and 0.4 seconds per step, with an ease-out
  curve (`rate_functions.ease_out_cubic`): the motion starts fast and settles.
  Long animations make the audience wait for the slide.
- **No pause at the end.** A step ends when its motion ends; a trailing
  `self.wait()` only delays the next click.
- **No decoration.** Every element on screen is part of the explanation.
- **The slide's colors.** Do not set `self.camera.background_color`: banners
  draws the scene on the slide's panel color. Take the colors of shapes and
  text from the palette, as `BLUE.primary` and `BLUE.text` above.

## Names that clash with banners

banners and Manim both export `Text`, and Manim's color constants (such as
`BLUE`) share names with the banners palettes. Import Manim's under another
name, as `from manim import Text as MText` above, so a marimo notebook does
not see two definitions of the same name.

## Scenes that follow any palette

A function that takes `palette` and returns a `Scene` class receives the
slide's palette from banners:

```python
from banners import Manim, Section
from manim import Circle, Create, Scene

def Dot(palette):
    class _Dot(Scene):
        def construct(self):
            self.play(Create(Circle(color=palette.primary)), run_time=0.3)
    return _Dot

Section(title="Follows the slide", content=[Manim(Dot)])
```

`banners.scenes.PipelineScene` is built this way.
